did_you_know.text: The phrase “a false report” means a rumor that is untrue or unfounded. The verse suggests that false testimony can begin with spreading a rumor.
The verse warns that a majority is not automatically proof of what is right. Even in court, truth is not decided simply by counting supporters.
“You shall surely help him” is understood as practical help in unloading the animal, not merely feeling pity. The Torah thus turns even personal hostility into an opportunity to do good.
The word “bribe” refers to a gift meant to influence a decision. The Torah stresses that even a clever person may unconsciously distort judgment after receiving a benefit.
The day of rest is meant not only for people: the verse explicitly includes animals and resident foreigners. It presents the ancient idea that everyone who works needs rest.
“The month of Aviv” is a seasonal description of the month when grain begins to ripen, not the ancient name of Nisan. The name Nisan became common later.

The pilgrimage festivals are linked to different stages of the agricultural year: grain harvest, gathering the crops, and bringing in the produce. The festival calendar therefore connects historical memory with life on the land.

The prohibition against cooking a kid in its mother’s milk appears three times in the Torah. In rabbinic times it became the basis for a broader separation of meat and dairy, while the original wording specifically mentions a kid, milk, and cooking together.
The word “malakh” primarily means a messenger or envoy. The word itself does not require imagining a winged figure; that image developed in later traditions.
The word translated as “hornet” is not completely certain in this context. In ancient sources, it was understood as a symbol of fear or a force that drives enemies away.

The verse presents gradual settlement as an environmental consideration: a population that is too small could not cultivate the land, and wild animals might multiply there. It is an example of thinking about the unintended effects of sudden change.
